target_customer: Allergy clinics and doctors' offices that use a point-of-care fingerstick IgE test
problem: Disease and allergy testing normally needs a venous blood draw and a lab; Kenota built an automated point-of-care fingerstick system for total IgE results in under 30 minutes.
business_model: Diagnostic instrument plus consumable test cartridges sold to clinics

founders.name: Moufeed Kaddoura
previous_startups: Ranata Therapeutics (CEO, listed on YC page as current role)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO, former founder, now CEO of Ranata Therapeutics. Education not found.

founders.name: Eric Blondeel
previous_startups: Samos Insurance (W22, listed on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Founder/CTO; education not found. Chris Harder appeared as CTO in 2023 and 2024 company releases per a directory page.

exit.reason: YC lists the company as inactive; no announcement, bankruptcy or post-mortem was found and the kenota.com domain no longer belongs to the company.

competitors.name: Genalyte
competitors.what: Single fingertip blood test using silicon photonic sensors, described as another Theranos competitor

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to build a hardware instrument and assay chemistry that delivers lab-grade IgE from capillary blood, then pass FDA 510(k) and CLIA waiver review. Clearance came in May 2024, about eight years after the batch.

defensibility.rationale: FDA 510(k) clearance with a CLIA waiver (K231151) and a trademark on KENOTA create real barriers, though only one cleared analyte (total IgE) was found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it. Fingerstick testing was in public doubt after Theranos.

market_need_then: Allergy testing usually needs a venous draw and lab turnaround; the 2020 press says clinics could test in under 30 minutes. No independent 2016 demand source was found, and the Theranos collapse made fingerstick claims harder to sell.

branding.domain_note: Used kenota.com; the domain has expired and now resolves to an unrelated site.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical; company tagline 'Kenota is revolutionizing the way we test for disease'.

rebrands.why: Not stated; USPTO trademark filing for KENOTA dated 2020-02-12, and a December 2020 article already uses the new name.

brand_strength.rationale: Some trade press at the Series A and FDA clearance, but no consumer or community signal. The rebrand from the generic ExVivo Labs to an invented name was sensible.

outcome_analysis: Kenota raised about $11M in total across a 2016 seed and a 2020 Series A led by Draper Associates and won FDA 510(k) clearance with a CLIA waiver for its Kenota 1 total IgE test in May 2024. YC lists it as inactive and its website lapsed, but no announcement, bankruptcy filing or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: The 2016 seed of about $2M and its investor list rest on a single directory page (healthcarediscovery.ai, citing a Golden wiki entry from 2018); Dealroom shows a $125K seed, so the amount is uncertain. The Series A is $9M in the Communitech and Private Capital Journal headlines and the 2020 release says total funding was $11M including the $2M seed (the Rosenman Institute headline says $11M); CB Insights shows $7.03M on 2020-12-07 and $12.61M total over 5 rounds; the only SEC Form D (August 2018) shows $5,296,435 sold of a $12,104,996 offering, which no later filing reconciles. Series A date is December 2020 per the announcement; the directory page says it closed August 31, 2020. Company website kenota.com is expired and does not belong to the company. Headquarters differ between Waterloo and Kitchener, Ontario.
